# Native core app kit 1.0.0

Real and packaged fake HTML hosts deliver this admitted release when author
source opts in with the inert policy below. The host installs frozen
`window.native.kit` synchronously before the first author script. Major 1 defaults
to 1.0.0. An unavailable requested major refuses `kit_major_unavailable` before
publication; use a major admitted by the host.

```html
<script type="application/json" id="native-app-kit">{"schema":"native.app-kit.v1","major":1}</script>
```

Selection belongs to the host. Each prepared document retains its exact release;
a fresh launch or reload uses the host's current compatible selection. Restoring
author source restores its policy, independently of host release history.
Documents without opt-in keep the legacy bridge and have no supplied kit.

## Prepare an install from Native MCP alone

Create the complete HTML as a `Document/artifact` with runtime `native.html.v1`.
Use its write receipt's `body_digest` (or body-carrying `source_event_id`) to call
`artifacts_read.manage_alpha_tabs.prepare_install` through `call_executor`:

```json
{"executor":"artifacts_read","operation":"manage_alpha_tabs.prepare_install","arguments":{"artifact_id":"<source id>","expected_body_digest":"<body_digest>","package":"agent.my-app","version":"1.0.0","declaration":{"needs":[],"effects":[]},"reason":"Install my authored app"}}
```

Include your actual consent declaration, including each SQL snapshot need.
When `ready` is true, pass the returned `next_call` to `call_executor`, adding
your `run_key`. It contains the server-computed digests, source revision and
install/update event precondition; no shell, hash computation or build is needed.
When false, read the bounded findings, fix the source/declaration and prepare again.
Malformed package/version/reason/request/guard arguments and authority failures
are normal API errors, rather than `ready:false` findings. Preparation caps the
echoed declaration at 65,536 serialized JSON bytes; `require_declaration` has
entry limits but no total byte cap. An optional `request` is validated and passed
through, including a reinstall over a removed tab; updates must preserve it.
Kit availability is advisory against the packaged default; delivery checks its
own selection. Preparation grants nothing, installs nothing and locks nothing.
The returned revision pins historical bytes; later source edits do not silently
replace them. Re-prepare after edits. Current update CAS and consent rules still
apply. `ready:true` means prepared, not usable. Read `adoption`: when it is
`requires_person_preview_adopt`, tell the signed-in person to Preview/Adopt after
install/update; MCP cannot mint that authority. `carried` means the update can
carry proven adoption for an unchanged canonical declaration. An unadopted
predecessor still requires Preview/Adopt even when the declaration is unchanged.

Alpha tabs pin a package/version/digest, a viewable live `Document/artifact`, its
source revision and consented needs/effects. Updates check exact bytes/digest and
event CAS, preserving status/request. Keyed retries return the original receipt
and current install without reapplying. Disable/restore/remove use event CAS;
disabled or removed tabs stop reads/actions. Target resolution fails closed;
inspect `target_resolves`. List before reorder: reorder replaces the strip order,
appends omitted installs, and refuses unknown/removed/duplicate entries. Without
a saved order, the strip uses agents/folders/tasks/graph/installs.

Preview checks exact source/digest and returns sample HTML with an expiring
account/pin/session receipt; it writes nothing. Preview/adopt/adopt_authored
require a hosted cookie and trusted Origin, never Bearer credentials. Adopt
checks the receipt, pin, event and attestation. Launch checks adoption, event,
View and source; its one-use URL delivers sample input only, without live rows.
`live_read` returns only the caller's authorized consented inputs:
`attention.query.v1` at `input.records`, up to eight `sql.snapshot.v1` SELECT/WITH
needs with 200 rows each at `input.sql[key]`. `params[0]` binds `?1`; omitted
optional parameters bind NULL. Use `live_read.need` to request a consented `records.search.v1` with
`params:{query,limit}` (`limit` at most 30), `records.resolve_reference.v1` with
`params:{reference}`, or a SQL need by key with its declared parameter schema.
Omit `need` for the snapshot. Subscriptions are connection-bound; use the stream-frame token;
subscriptions and `if_revision` apply only to snapshot reads. An `if_revision`
equal to `revision_digest` returns `unchanged:true` with pins/revision and no rows.
Use `if_revision` to resynchronize. Revision information includes `id` and
`time_dependent`; `now_ms()` uses `as_of_ms`. `subscribe_refused` includes the
read. `live_unsubscribe` is idempotent and connection-scoped.
`admit_reveal_target` checks consented `surface.reveal.v1` and one visible
canonical target/pin; delivery is push-only, never via `live_read`.
Supply the full record id or a reserved id such as `native:root`; prefixes refuse.

Apps own their DOM and CSS. Declare each exact param-less `sql.snapshot.v1` need
in the app policy. The kit reads only delivered declared snapshots; it adds no
data grant and offers no parameterized reads, watches, writes, Body/editor,
rendering, network, or session capability. Link helpers return attributes; the
host validates navigation and requires trusted user activation.

Release metadata identifies the reviewed JS and types. These hashes are package
custody identities, not app permission or consent digests. The catalog retains
admitted releases; a separate bounded host selector chooses an exact release
for each requested major. No runtime download or author-supplied release path
is used. After admission these versioned bytes must be retained; changes require
a new reviewed release.

The exact types below retain their admitted SHA-256 identity, including the
historical preparation-era comment saying hosted delivery was unavailable.
That comment is release provenance; this guide describes current delivery.
`Host.kit` remains optional because unhosted and non-opted-in documents lack it.
Negotiated v2 methods can coexist on `window.native`, but are unavailable before
host negotiation and are outside this core kit's type/capability contract.

```js
const kit = window.native?.kit;
if (!kit) throw new Error('Native core kit is unavailable');
await kit.ready;
const count = document.querySelector('#count');
const status = document.querySelector('#status');
const stop = kit.subscribe('records.recent', feed => {
  if (feed.status === 'ready' && count) {
    count.textContent = kit.countLabel(feed.result);
    // Render rows with DOM/textContent and app-owned styling.
  } else if (feed.status === 'error' && status) {
    status.textContent = kit.errorText(feed.error);
    // feed.last can remain visible, explicitly marked as last-good.
  }
});
addEventListener('pagehide', stop, { once: true });
```

`ready` rejects on bridge readiness failure. A missing declared key refuses
`undeclared`; malformed results refuse `malformed`. Each valid replacement may
notify. Subscriptions emit loading, then ready/error, retaining last-good data
on errors. Cleanup is idempotent and prevents further callbacks. There is no
app-facing lifecycle disposal or registration capability.

Release `1.0.0`, major `1`, layer `core`. Factory `native.app-kit.core.factory.v1`; bridge `native.html.bridge.v1`.

JS SHA-256: `7530fc7e42fb1551acadc67d048af75dadf61be94daa881ffe67d79a41f06a8e`

Types SHA-256: `c5a4481cb2613b98d4454aee483c1ad3d974b873f0684037c555e62ed0a2a742`

```typescript
// Native core app kit — AGPL-3.0-only; Copyright Native contributors.
// Release 1.0.0; major 1; native.app-kit.core.factory.v1; native.html.bridge.v1
declare namespace NativeAppKit {
  interface KitRelease {
      readonly version: string;
      readonly major: number;
      readonly layer: "core";
      readonly factory: "native.app-kit.core.factory.v1";
      readonly bridge: "native.html.bridge.v1";
      readonly js_sha256: string;
      readonly types_sha256: string;
  }

  /** One result row, keyed by output column name. */
  type Row = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

  /**
   * One capped answer. `rows` is what was delivered; `truncated` says the
   * answer is a prefix. `rowCount` is a total only while `rowCountComplete` is
   * true, otherwise it is a floor ("more than N"). An app must show both.
   */
  interface QueryResult {
      readonly label: string;
      readonly columns: readonly string[];
      readonly rows: readonly Row[];
      readonly rowCount: number;
      readonly rowCountComplete: boolean;
      readonly truncated: boolean;
      /**
       * Set only on a result the host served from its cache, ahead of the
       * revalidation that follows it (a remount). It clears on the next uncached
       * delivery, even if the rows are equal. The host sends nothing for a
       * revalidation that finds equal rows, so then the flag stays set: do not
       * treat it as proof the rows are stale, only as "served from cache".
       */
      readonly cached?: boolean;
      /**
       * Set only on the `last` rows of an error feed whose subscription has ended
       * for good (a terminal error): nothing will refresh them, so they may be out
       * of date. They are kept for display; do not present them as current.
       */
      readonly stale?: boolean;
      /**
       * Only for the host-pushed keyed needs (`HOST_PUSHED_KEYED_NEEDS`): the
       * opaque handle the host minted for this parameter variant. The host names
       * it in `keyed_freshness.changed` when the variant's rows move.
       */
      readonly variant?: string;
  }

  /** Why a port call failed. Stable, app-facing; adapters map their transport onto it. */
  type PortErrorCode = "busy" | "timeout" | "undeclared" | "refused" | "unavailable" | "malformed" | "closed";

  /** Stable diagnostic shape; no transport or write capability. */
  interface KitError extends Error {
      readonly code: PortErrorCode;
      readonly detail?: string;
  }

  /** What a live subscription is showing right now. Errors keep the last good result. */
  type Feed<T> = {
      readonly status: "loading";
  } | {
      readonly status: "ready";
      readonly result: T;
  } | {
      readonly status: "error";
      readonly error: KitError;
      readonly last?: T;
  };

  /** Apps own DOM and CSS; all data comes from their declared snapshots. */
  interface CoreKit {
      readonly release: KitRelease;
      readonly ready: Promise<void>;
      read(key: string): Promise<QueryResult>;
      subscribe(key: string, listener: (feed: Feed<QueryResult>) => void): () => void;
      countLabel(result: QueryResult): string;
      errorText(error: Pick<KitError, "code">): string;
      recordLink(id: string): {
          readonly "data-native-record-id": string;
      };
      externalLink(url: string): {
          readonly "data-native-external-url": string;
      };
  }

  /** Optional because hosted delivery of this release is not available yet. */
  interface Host {
      readonly kit?: CoreKit;
  }
}
interface Window { readonly native?: NativeAppKit.Host }
```
